sourcedFrom: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip straight out of Staccato's own C instructions: slide stop lever down, slide stop out, slide forward off the frame, then the guide rod drawn forward by its flange and down off the barrel, the guide rod and reverse plug out the back of the slide, and the barrel out the front. ⛔ This is not the strip for the Staccato C2, CS, P, XC or XL — each has its own recoil step.

steps.title: Muzzle in a safe direction
steps.action: Start with the pistol pointed somewhere safe and keep it that way through the whole strip. Staccato opens the C procedure with this before anything else is touched, because the next step works the slide.
steps.quote: Ensure the pistol is pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Racked, then chamber and magazine well both checked
steps.action: Rack the slide to the rear and look into the chamber and into the magazine well — both places, not one. An empty chamber over a loaded magazine is still a loaded pistol the moment the slide goes forward again.
steps.quote: Rack the slide to the rear and visually inspect the chamber and magazine well to make sure the pistol's empty.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Takedown notch lined up with the slide stop knuckle
steps.action: The slide stop is what holds the top end on the lower, so it comes out first. Draw the slide back until the takedown notch sits over the knuckle of the slide stop and hold it there. If the notch is off the knuckle, the slide stop will not come out cleanly.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to line up to take down notch on the slide with the slide stop knuckle.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Slide stop lever pushed all the way down against the frame
steps.action: With the notch held on the knuckle, push down on the slide stop lever until it sits all the way down against the frame. A lever left part-way up is what makes the slide stop bind on the way out.
steps.quote: Push down on the slide stop lever to ensure its lowered down all the way against your frame,
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Slide stop pin pushed from the opposite side, slide stop out
steps.action: Push the slide stop pin from the far side of the pistol with a finger or a small tool, and take the slide stop out. It should move under light pressure; if it resists, the notch has drifted off the knuckle or the lever is not fully down.
steps.quote: push on the slide stop pin on the opposite side of your pistol using your finger or a small tool to remove the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide gently forward and off the frame rails. Gently is Staccato's word — the slide carries the barrel, guide rod and reverse plug with it, and nothing on this step needs force.
steps.quote: Gently pull the slide forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Guide rod forward by its flange, then down off the barrel
steps.action: Take the guide rod by its flange, pull it forward slightly, then bring it down off the barrel. The flange sits against the barrel, and it has to clear forward before it will drop.
steps.quote: Remove the guide rod by pulling the flange forward slightly and then down off of the barrel.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Guide rod and reverse plug out the back of the slide
steps.action: Draw the guide rod and the reverse plug out of the back of the slide. This is the C's own recoil step — they come out the back, not the front. Keep the two together so neither goes missing on the bench.
steps.quote: Remove the guide rod and the reverse plug out of the back of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Link forward, barrel out of the muzzle end
steps.action: Slide the link forward, then draw the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide. That completes the strip — frame, slide stop, slide, guide rod, reverse plug and barrel. Staccato publishes nothing further than this for the C.
steps.quote: Slide the link forward and pull the barrel out from the muzzle end of your slide.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly

steps.title: Rails, frame surfaces and feed ramp brushed and wiped
steps.action: With a brush attachment, a rag or a paper towel, clear the debris off the slide rails, the frame surfaces and the feed ramp.
steps.prose: The feed ramp is the one most often skipped. Carbon there is where feeding trouble starts, and the rails carry the grit the slide rides on every shot.
steps.quote: Use your brush attachment or a rag or a paper towel to clean away debris from the slide rails, frame surfaces and feed ramp.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Bore brushed breech to muzzle on the memory flex cable
steps.action: Pull the bore brush through the barrel on the memory flex cable, from the breech to the muzzle, and repeat as needed.
steps.prose: Breech to muzzle carries the fouling out the front instead of back into the chamber.
steps.quote: Use your bore brush to clean the bore of your barrel, utilizing the memory flex cable and pulling it from breech to muzzle.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Bore oiled with the mop
steps.action: Put a small amount of CLP on the bore mop and oil the bore.
steps.prose: A small amount is the instruction — the next step wipes back out whatever the mop leaves behind.
steps.quote: Apply a small amount of CLP to your bore mop, and oil the bore of your barrel.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Excess oil wiped out with a clean patch
steps.action: Run a clean patch through the barrel to take the excess oil back out of the bore.
steps.prose: The point is a film of oil in the bore, not a wet one.
steps.quote: Using a clean patch, wipe away excess oil from the inside of your barrel.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: A few drops on the slide rails and barrel contact points
steps.action: Put a few drops of lubricant on the slide rails and on the barrel's contact points, and no more.
steps.prose: Staccato says a few drops. More than that does not make the pistol run better — it holds powder residue and grit where the slide and barrel move.
steps.quote: Apply a few drops of lubricant to your slide rails and barrel contact points.
steps.cite: Staccato C Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

deepAbsentReason: Staccato publishes this page as basic disassembly and reassembly — the article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato C', and it ends at frame, slide stop, slide, guide rod, reverse plug and barrel. No extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip procedure is published on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. For any other maintenance or disassembly question, the page directs owners to contact Staccato directly. Nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: RAILS, FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush and wipe debris off the slide rails
Brush and wipe the frame surfaces

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Pull the bore brush from breech to muzzle on the memory flex cable, repeating as needed
Put a small amount of CLP on a bore mop and oil the bore
Wipe the excess oil out of the barrel with a clean patch

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A few drops of lubricant on the slide rails
A few drops on the barrel contact points

reassembly: Check the link is flipped forward toward the muzzle, then reinstall the barrel.
Insert the recoil system into the spring tunnel of the slide and align it against the barrel lugs.

Line the slide rails up with the frame rails and run the slide on. Staccato's own note: the guide rod flange must be pushed up all the way against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must not be rotated to either side, or the top end will not slide fully onto the lower.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the pin on the slide stop must pass through the hole in the link or the pistol will not function properly. If it is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop into the frame through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the knuckle on the slide stop, then seat the slide stop fully into the frame.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide several times and confirm it returns fully into battery, then check the slide stop is fully seated in the frame — a slide stop that will not seat has missed the hole in the barrel link.
